correctness.rationale: Direct ring multiplication yields [a+bu,c+du]=(d(1-sigma)a-b(1-sigma)c)u; its exact linear equations give center, all q+2 centralizers, clique partition and each commutator fiber. A common finite-field fixed field implies same im(1-sigma) for generators of the same cyclic Galois subgroup. Inverting difference maps on a common complement yields a bijective additive commutator intertwiner; converse follows from the centers and quotient sizes. The radical and residue-field relation proves distinct and inverse twists are respectively nonisomorphic and anti-isomorphic. Verified full finite arithmetic tables over eight field/twist cases, plus explicit F32 intertwiner. Computation is illustrative, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The original scoped content is the iff fixed-field equivalence for all additive commutators, complete class-specific centralizers and word-map fibers, and nonisomorphic/nonantiisomorphic collisions. Raghavendran already classifies underlying twisted matrix rings; Kinyon repeats the sharp zero-divisor bound; Dutta2019 covers the generic CC-ring graph decomposition; Dutta2017 covers the generic isoclinism graph implication. These are acknowledged and not claimed as novel. Comparisons of actual mathematical implications and focused published-finding corpus searches identified no source covering the new conjunction or structural criterion. Older unindexed equivalent formulations remain possible.

value.rationale: The family is natural in recent work on extremizers for finite-zero-divisor cardinality bounds. The precise fixed-field criterion is a complete invariant for commutator equivalence but strictly weaker than ring isomorphism or anti-isomorphism, exhibiting infinite families of distinct multiplication structures invisible even to entire commutator word distributions. Exact centralizers and fibers quantify the loss of information and supply natural computable invariants for every finite field; this is more than a routine single parameter computation.
